12 = Plut. 28, cod. 34. — Membran., cm. 26 × 21, ff. 1-170 (24v vac.). Adiecta
sunt II folia chartac. in principio, III in fine, saec. XI (cf. tamen infra ad f. 143v). —
Fol. Iv index latinus inabsolutus. Inter fol. 56 et 57 multa interciderunt : vide
infra. Post f. 108 v videtur folium excidisse „ [Kroll]. Post f. 129 duo folia desunt
et ea media quaternionis (recte rec. manus infra scripsit: λείπει φῦλλα βʹ) „ Wachs-
muth, p. XIX. — Ex indice latino praefixo apparet hunc librum fine mutilum
esse atque duo folia deesse videntur. Legebatur olim “ Prophetia de fine machu-
meticae sectae quo anno erunt quinque planetes in bonis signo (sic ?) quae est ad
chartas huius libri 171 id est ροαʹ „ (cf. cod. 7, f. 240). — Codicem inabsolutissime
descripsit Bandini, II, p. 59-62; eiusdem “ indicem non plenum quidem sed multo
pleniorem Bandiniano „ dedit Ludwich, pp. 125. 6. Cf. Wachsmuth, p. XIV,
Engelbrecht, p. 12 ss. Nuperrime W. Kroll (Philologus, 1898, p. 123 sqq.) de astro-
logis quibus opera huius libri tribuenda sint, disseruit; quorum commentariorum
praecipua in usum nostrum concedente auctore transtulimus.
sections.en:
12 = Plut. 28, cod. 34. — Parchment, 26 × 21 cm, ff. 1-170 (24v blank). Added
are II paper folios at the beginning, III at the end, 11th century (cf. however below at f. 143v). —
Fol. Iv incomplete Latin index. Between fol. 56 and 57 many things have fallen out: see
below. After f. 108 v a folio seems to have fallen out „ [Kroll]. After f. 129 two folios are missing
and those in the middle of a quaternion (correctly a recent hand wrote below: 2 folios are missing) „ Wachs-
muth, p. XIX. — From the prefixed Latin index it appears that this book is mutilated at the end
and two folios seem to be missing. It was once read “ Prophecy concerning the end of the Maho-
metan sect in which year there will be five planets in good signs (sic ?) which is at
folios 171 of this book that is 171 „ (cf. cod. 7, f. 240). — The codex was very incompletely
described by Bandini, II, p. 59-62; his “ index not full indeed but much
fuller than Bandini's „ Ludwich gave, pp. 125. 6. Cf. Wachsmuth, p. XIV,
Engelbrecht, p. 12 ss. Most recently W. Kroll (Philologus, 1898, p. 123 sqq.) concerning the astro-
logers to whom the works of this book are to be attributed, discussed; of whose commentaries
we have translated the principal ones for our use with the author conceding.

summary.headline: Astrological Questions and Martial Elections
summary.text: Catalogue entries 136–148 covering passionate places and enigmatic zodiac signs, harmful degrees affecting the eyes, lunar applications and separations, bodily conjunctions, tyranny, lost things, ruined or besieged cities, martial elections and warfare, and mundane effects of eclipse nodes and right and left configurations. The apparatus identifies Plut. 28, cod. 34 and cites Bandini, Ludwich, Wachsmuth, Engelbrecht, and W. Kroll.
